method: Two kinds of score exist, and every score on screen says which it is:
STATS: built from real IPL career statistics (below) for players with enough IPL batting or bowling data.

ESTIMATED ("est."): for players with no usable IPL record (new, uncapped or very few matches). Starting point = the median strength of newer (30 matches or fewer), stats-rated players of the same role, blended halfway with the overall median so no role is unfairly penalised. Bonus up to +9 for the price the franchise paid at the 2026 auction (+2.2 per natural-log step above ₹0.3 Cr), +0.4 per IPL match played (max +4), and up to ±5 for how the little he has played compares with other IPL players (strike rate / runs for batting, economy / wickets for bowling; full weight only from 90 balls). Always kept between 35 and 66.
Team strength = the average of all its purchased players’ scores (stats and estimates together).
Every figure is computed from IPL ball-by-ball data (Cricsheet.org, 2008 to the latest season).
Batting (qualifies with 100+ balls faced): batting average 22%, strike rate 22%, total runs 22%, milestones (100s count double 50s) 17%, boundaries (fours + 1.5 x sixes) 17%.
Bowling (qualifies with 120+ balls bowled): wickets 25%, economy 25%, bowling average 20%, bowling strike rate 15%, best figures 15%.
Fielding: catches + 2 x stumpings + run outs, per match.
Each statistic is ranked as a percentile against every qualifying IPL player (lower is better for bowling average, economy and strike rate).
Role weights: Batter 90/10 batting/fielding; Wicketkeeper 75/25 batting/keeping; All-rounder 45/45/10 batting/bowling/fielding; Bowler 90/10 bowling/fielding.
Players with fewer than 30 IPL matches are pulled toward 50 in proportion to how short their record is.
A player with no usable IPL record is "unrated" and is left out of team averages.
